VALIDATED 2026-10-07: F21 (M2 fix feature F21-m2-verse-manifest-race, from M1 user-testing round 1) fixes the verse-manifest open race at the SEAM, not the relay instance. fe-sync sync_thread.rs no longer warn-and-drops a WriteRowEntry whose verse replica is not open yet — it retains the write in a bounded PendingWrites queue (cap 1024, drop-oldest + warn) and handle_open_verse_replica republishes the verse's queue in FIFO order through the same write path a live write takes after a successful open. A failed online open never flushes (F20's loud non-replicating state publishes nothing; writes stay retained for a later successful re-open), and sync-thread shutdown drops still-retained writes with a warn (process-lifetime retention). Why: create_verse_handler emits the manifest ReplicationEvent ~100ms BEFORE the host's VerseCreated/navigation OpenVerseReplica reaches the sync thread, so the first manifest row warn-and-dropped and never entered the doc — seed_reconciliation cannot heal a row that never entered, so a fresh relay's doc permanently lacked its verse manifest and a fresh peer joining never received it, defeating A3's bootstrap window. Both hosts fixed by construction (relay replicas.rs VerseCreated system; GUI navigation_manager open_replica — new fe-ui test navigation_to_created_verse_sends_open_verse_replica pins the GUI open path, dev-dep fe-identity added to fe-ui for the in-memory secret-store fixture). FUTURE-OPS 2026-10-07 (second M1 user-testing round-1 finding, recorded per conductor directive; invite-generation-over-REST/MCP and secret persistence are OUT of current mission scope — deferred, NOT scheduled, and this note is the tracking home): relay REST-created verses have process-lifetime secrets. create_verse_handler generates the namespace secret into the process's EnvBackend in-memory override only (no persistence, no invite-extraction route), so after a relay restart such verses' replicas can never re-open — the secret dies with the process and no route can hand it to a second relay or a joining peer (the GUI persists its secrets to the OS keystore, so the GUI path is unaffected). Operator workaround until the deferred work lands: env-inject FE_SECRET_FRACTALENGINE_VERSE_<ULID>_NS_SECRET_FRACTALENGINE (64 hex) for verses that must survive restarts, or seed verses with the operator-owned secret via the fe-database examples/seed_join_verse fixture. F17 (M7 close-out) will document this workaround plainly in the relay README ops surface.
VALIDATED 2026-10-07: F5 (assertions A11+A12) starts the timeseries fabric: iot_reading ingestion now publishes replication. New fe-database handler insert_readings_with_replication (insert_readings is a delegating shim) validates the whole batch, inserts durably, THEN emits one ReplicationEvent per accepted row carrying verse_id (derived from the resolved petal scope by the caller), petal_id, table=iot_reading and record_id=reading_id, with the row bytes content-addressed through the shared blob store - a peer never sees a row the local store cannot serve. fe-api/src/iot.rs calls it on the db_reader path with ApiState.replication_tx + ApiState.blob_store; a None in either degrades to durable-but-unpublished with one warn per batch (never a failed ingest). Both binaries wire the seam: GUI main.rs passes replication_tx + blob_store_for_api, relay main.rs passes repl_tx_for_api (both were already wired at F4). New fe-database/src/replication_mode.rs: ReplicationMode::{Row,Timeseries} with for_table (iot_reading = Timeseries, every other table = Row) - canonical in fe-database because the inbound applier must dispatch on it, re-exported by fe-sync so producers share one definition instead of two that can drift. handlers/replicated_row.rs dispatches per table AFTER the A3 gate (admission precedes mode dispatch, so union semantics never widen authority): Timeseries takes apply_timeseries_row - insert only when the reading_id is absent, never overwrite (a conflicting payload reports Applied with the local value intact, matching the node path whose idempotent re-merge also reports Applied), and an empty Doc::del entry is NotApplicable so a timeseries fact is never tombstoned; Row keeps the tombstone-aware merge. Union semantics are covered at the data layer (fe-database A12 tests: re-delivery idempotent, conflicting payload never overwrites, order-independence, empty entry never removes the fact, viewer denied) and end-to-end by the new harness scenario 10 two_peer_timeseries_sync over the real loopback transport (identical re-delivery stays one row; a conflicting payload does not overwrite; an empty-entry tombstone is NotApplicable with the row still present; an earlier-timestamped reading delivered later still joins the set). REPLY CORRELATION (the F4 handoff hazard): fe-runtime/src/app.rs PendingApiRequests no longer pairs replies FIFO. DbResult carries no correlation id and the DB thread also fans unsolicited results into the same channel (the relay startup scan HierarchyLoaded, GUI hierarchy reloads), so arrival order could cross-pair a racing /ready Ping with a HierarchyLoaded. The queue is now keyed by reply family (ReplyKind) via enqueue_for / reply_kind_of_command / reply_kind_of_result: a result only reaches the oldest waiter of its own family, DbResult::Error is the wildcard delivered to the oldest waiter of any family, and a result with no waiter is dropped rather than mis-delivered. Fire-and-forget commands must not enqueue a waiter - fe-api/src/rest.rs move_waypoint now sends ApiCommand::TransformPersist fire-and-forget (it previously registered a waiter the DB thread never answered, leaving a dangling entry later results could land in). Tests: 5 new fe-runtime app::tests (hierarchy never satisfies a Ping, same-kind FIFO preserved, Error reaches the oldest waiter, no-waiter result dropped, mapping consistency for every awaited command); the hazard and the maintenance rules are documented in fe-runtime/src/AGENTS.md §api-reply-correlation. FOLD-IN: the stale namespace_id_from_secret doc comment in fractalengine-relay/src/replicas.rs (still describing the pre-F20 keyed-BLAKE3 derivation) now documents the delegation to fe_database::derive_namespace_id (Ed25519 verifying key) and warns against reintroducing the keyed-BLAKE3 form. Docs: fe-database/src/AGENTS.md gained §replication-mode plus the §iot-readings emit-seam paragraph; fe-api/AGENTS.md §iot-ingest documents the API emit seam and its main.rs wiring; fe-test-harness/src/AGENTS.md gained scenario 10. Evidence: cargo test -p fe-database 184 passed 0 failed (11 pre-existing ignores) with integration suites green (iot_reading 13); cargo test -p fe-api 88 passed with integration suites green (iot_ingest 6 - 2 new A11 tests: one event per row with verse+petal on the db_reader path, and no seam = durable rows with no events); cargo test -p fe-runtime 66 + 13 passed (7 app::tests); cargo test -p fe-sync 152 passed; cargo clippy -p fe-database -p fe-api -p fe-runtime -p fe-sync -p fractalengine-relay --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean; harness 12 passed 0 failed (FE_SYNC_RELAY=disabled) including the new A12 scenario. Residual (recorded honestly): there is no DbCommand that ingests readings, so the DB-thread half of A11 is the handler seam itself (the same function the DB thread calls with its own blob store + replication sender, proven by the fe-database seam tests); a DbCommand::InsertIotReadings would let a DB-thread-driven scenario exercise that leg over the transport and is the natural shape if the UI ever ingests. Keep in_progress; n0 hosted-relay EOL remains 2026-12-31.
